questions.question: What comes next? 3, 8, 13, 18, ?
questions.explain: The gap between each number is 5. So 18 plus 5 is 23. A common trap is to go back to the first number or to miscount the gap.

questions.question: What comes next? 10, 15, 20, 25, ?
questions.explain: Each number grows by 5. 25 plus 5 is 30. The pattern keeps growing — it does not loop back to 10.

questions.question: What comes next? 5, 12, 19, 26, ?
questions.explain: Count the gap: 12 minus 5 is 7. So 26 plus 7 is 33. Checking the gap more than once helps you be sure.

questions.question: What comes next? 14, 19, 24, 29, ?
questions.explain: The gap is 5 each time. 29 plus 5 is 34. The pattern keeps growing — it does not go back to 14.

questions.question: Maya picks up 4 seashells on Monday, 9 on Tuesday, 14 on Wednesday, and 19 on Thursday. How many on Friday?
questions.explain: Each day Maya picks up 5 more than the day before. 19 plus 5 is 24. The number keeps going up — it does not start over at 4.

questions.question: Sam steps on tile 6, then 11, then 16, then 21. Which tile is his next step?
questions.explain: Each step lands on a tile 5 higher than the last. 21 plus 5 is 26. The steps keep going up — they do not jump back to tile 6.

questions.question: Leo writes the pattern 8, 13, 18, 23 on his homework. What number comes next?
questions.explain: The gap is 5: 13 minus 8 is 5. So 23 plus 5 is 28. The pattern grows — it does not loop back to 8.

questions.question: Nina saves 12 coins on day one, 18 on day two, 24 on day three, and 30 on day four. How many on day five?
questions.explain: Each day Nina saves 6 more coins. 30 plus 6 is 36. The number keeps growing — it does not go back to 12.

questions.question: A pattern is 7, __, 19, 25. One number is missing. What is it?
questions.explain: First find the gap: 25 minus 19 is 6. Then 19 minus 6 is 13. Check: 13 minus 6 is 7. The whole row works!

questions.question: Ben has 6 marbles on day one and 11 on day two. Each day he gets 5 more. How many on day five?
questions.explain: Each day adds 5 more. After day two (11), count up: 16, 21, 26. Day five is 26. Keep adding 5 from where you left off.

questions.question: Rita says the pattern 9, 16, 23, 30 should go: 30, 37, 9, 16. What is her mistake?
questions.explain: The gap is 7 each time, and the pattern keeps growing. After 37 it should be 44, not back to 9. Growing patterns do not loop.

questions.question: Zoe's homework says: 4, 10, 16, __, 28. One number is missing. What is it?
questions.explain: Find the gap: 10 minus 4 is 6. Then 16 plus 6 is 22. Check: 22 plus 6 is 28. The whole row works!
